subject: psychology
title: Research Methods: Non-Experimental Methods
welcome_lead: Observations, correlations, interviews, case studies — when experiments won't do.
meta_desc: A-Level Psychology non-experimental methods: observation, correlation, self-report, case study.
final_note: If you cannot manipulate, you can still measure carefully.

concepts.def: Watching behaviour where it normally happens.
Observation in structured setting (e.g. Strange Situation).
Statistical relationship between two co-varying variables.
Written self-report — open or closed items.
Spoken self-report — structured, unstructured or semi-structured.
In-depth study of one individual or small group (e.g. HM, Genie).

walkthroughs.body_html: Observations vary in naturalism, structure, covertness and participation. Behavioural categories must be operationalised. Time sampling records every n seconds; event sampling counts each occurrence. Inter-observer reliability should exceed +0.80.

A correlation coefficient runs from -1 to +1. +1 = perfect positive; 0 = no relationship; -1 = perfect negative. Correlation cannot establish cause: the third-variable problem and bidirectionality limit inference.

Questionnaires can use Likert scales, semantic differentials or open items. Interviews trade off depth (unstructured) against comparability (structured). Both suffer social desirability bias; case studies (e.g. HM, who had no new LTM after a 1953 operation) provide rare depth but cannot generalise.
